translation:
Here begins the holy Vani ||7||

1. Parabrahma has wedded Vani (the divine Word); through the whole universe rings the cry of victory. The four sources of birth have been made pure; the delusion of worldly existence is broken.

2. The reckonings of Yama, lord of death, have been struck out; the trade of hell has been wound up. The bonds of living beings are loosed; all attain liberation this time round.

3. Freed are all things unmoving and moving; freed are gods, men and serpents. Freed are the seven sages and the nine planets; freed are the great munis (sages) of the world.

4. Hari, Har (Shiva) and Brahma rejoice; in house after house there is festival. The surge of gladness is very great; we shall sing of the bridegroom of Vani.

5. At every door festive banners fly up; the doorways are hung with garlands and festoons. The universe is filled with flowers and blossom; all six seasons wear joy.

6. Sprinklings of divine sandal-paste fall; the clouds of all twelve months rejoice. The Panchajanya conch is blown; the worlds resound with its unceasing roar.

7. Narayan, the lord of Lakshmi, rejoices greatly within his heart. Shankar dances the tandav; its sweep spreads out through all the worlds.

8. Ganga breaks loose from the crown; the serpent Vasuki sways. Eighty-eight thousand sages are in delight, and Brahma recites the Vedas.

9. So long as Parabrahma, the husband of Vani, remained unwed, so long there was affliction and bondage, and not once any happiness.

10. Now the whole universe has become happy, now that Jagannath has wed as befits him. Joy and supreme bliss have come; affliction and great sorrow are broken.

11. The hard sorrows are broken; the soul has become pure. The forms of the eighty-four lakh species -- all those entanglements are wholly broken.

12. The imagining of the three worlds is broken; there is one joy alone. Victory to the Supreme Self, Parabrahma; victory, victory to the support of the universe.

13. Crores of universes are the horses of the wedding train; in house after house the four auspicious wedding rounds. There is no day nor night nor hour, no moment, no age, no fraction of time, no world's end.

14. No hunger, no thirst, no sleep; no anxiety, no household drudgery. All that moves and moves not is satisfied; there is happiness, supreme bliss, rejoicing.

15. Nothing else is wanted; everyone's searching is at an end. Parabrahma the King is seated on his throne, and before him his beloved saints.

16. Let all do japa (repetition) of his virtues -- he who bears the four-armed form. No other name is to be spoken with the mouth; recite only "Ram".

17. There is no fear of birth, old age or death; there is no other business at all. You alone are the Lord of the earth; all the saints rejoice.

Here the Vani is complete ||7||

End of the first vishram (resting-point) of the five-day parayan (recitation).
